examples.input: `config history` on the starting file (the import of the existing values)

results.1: exit 0; a, d, f, j and k are imported as strings ("yes", "1_000", "1:30", "Off", "2001-12-14"). b = 15, c = 17, e = 1000.0, g = Infinity, h = 31, i = null, m = "café 😀"
results.2: four arms: the same as route 1; one arm: the same, except that g is recorded as the string ".inf" instead of Infinity, and m is written with escape codes ("caf\u00e9 \ud83d\ude00")

results.1: exit 0; plain values, e.g. `a: yes # from .troupe/troupe.yml`, `c: 17 …`, `g: .inf …`, `j: Off …`
results.2: four arms: output identical to route 1; one arm: string values are shown in quotes: `a: 'yes'`, `d: '1_000'`, `f: '1:30'`, `j: 'Off'`, `k: '2001-12-14'`

context.in_practice: Both routes read the file the same way: `yes`/`Off` stay text, `017` is 17 and `0o17` is 15. In both routes, every arm leaves untouched lines and comments byte-for-byte as they were. The only differences are what a `set` writes and some small display differences. Route 1's single arm, and two of route 2's five arms, write your value exactly as typed. The other three route 2 arms rewrite numbers in a normalized form (`0o20` becomes `16`, `1e3` becomes `1000.0`).
context.stakes: When you set a value through the CLI, the question is whether the YAML file gets exactly what you typed or a re-rendered version of it. The other question is whether existing values like `yes`, `017` or `.inf` are typed the same way when they are read back.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 needs its own typing rules on top of a library built for an older YAML version. Route 2 gets those rules from its library, but its arms were inconsistent: three normalized the numbers you typed, one recorded `.inf` as text, and one quoted strings in `show`.

plan_why: Shows which YAML rules each parser actually applies (YAML 1.1 vs 1.2 core) by loading and setting tricky values: yes/Off, 0o17, 017, 1_000, 1e3, 1:30, .inf, 0x1F, ~ and a date. Also checks byte-exact write-back next to a non-ASCII value and an end-of-line comment.
routes: PyYAML compose for node positions, with custom YAML 1.2 core resolution
ruamel.yaml compose only (nodes and marks); never use its dumper
